newsitem.title: USA: CommScope sees charge from Australian ops.
newsitem.headline: CommScope sees charge from Australian ops.

text.p: CommScope Inc said on Friday that it may post a charge related to its 49 percent owned Vision Cables Pty Ltd unit in Australia which is suspending manufacturing operations at its Melbourne facility this month.
CommScope and Pacific Dunlop Ltd, the co-owner of Vision Cables, said they are evaluating their future options for the facility, CommScope said in a statement.
If the operations are permanently discontinued, CommScope said it may need to post charges of $1 million to $3 million, or $0.02 to $0.06 a share, as early as the third quarter.
CommScope said Australia's cable TV markets have slowed in terms of construction activity after a two-year build out of cable systems in major markets.
Australia's coaxial cable market is becoming primarily a maintenance market that can be served by CommScope Exports and Vision Cables' distribution network, CommScope said.
Also, CommScope said it has reached a non-binding agreement with Alcatel Cable France that would establish a European base of operations for CommScope.
Alcatel would transfer to CommScope some of its coaxial cable busines in Belgium to CommScope and Alcatel would purchase its future coaxial cable requirements from CommScope, the company said.
In return, Alcatel would get substantially all of the assets from CommScope's high-temperature aerospace and industrial cable business in Elm City, North Carolina.
